title: New Residential Sales — new single-family home sales (October 2026 data), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 178 rows parsed), row "New Residential Sales | November 25, 2026 | 10:00 AM | October 2026", release code A202611251000, reference A202610. (2) construction/soc/schedule.html (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), the Survey of Construction program's own release-schedule table, whose "October 2026" row reads "November 18, 2026 | November 25, 2026" under the column header "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m." — the same shape of program-owned second primary the construction-spending-2026-12-01 and m3-full-report-2026-12-03 lanes used. Corroborated (not a Census source) by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-11-25 row reads "GDP (Q3 2nd estimate), Personal income and outlays, NIPA underlying detail tables, Advance Census manufacturing (M3-1), New-home sales". Promoted from the construction-spending-2026-12-01 lane's `estimate` proposal by this event's own initial research, on the precedent that lane set: the no-self-confirm convention binds the discovering sweep, not the independent second look. New Residential Sales has never been suspended — 84 consecutive reference months (2019-12 through 2026-11) with zero gaps across seven Census calendars, while the suspensions on those same pages belong to the Advance Economic Indicators Report, Preliminary Steel Imports and the Advance Services Report. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED by the construction-spending-2026-12-01 adjacency sweep as the demand-side read of the same October 2026 reference month. Initial research 2026-09-06 confirms the release identity and then measures both halves of the question, which is unusual for this family — this print is separable on the Atlanta Fed's model AND on the tape, and the two answers differ. On the model: GDPNow ContribArchives (1,871 vintages, 1,822 same-quarter deltas) shows vintages naming new-home sales alone (n=93) move |d residential| 0.0543pp against a 0.0058pp baseline (permutation p<0.0001, 9.4x), but move |d GDP| 0.0528pp against a 0.0961pp baseline (p=0.0287) — a new-home-sales day is a QUIETER headline-nowcast day than average. On 2026-11-25's exact shape (new-home sales bundled with personal income and outlays, n=13) the headline move belongs to Personal Income, not to this print: 0.4340pp vs 0.3404pp for personal-income-without-new-home-sales, p=0.5973, while the residential move stays this print's (0.0820pp vs 0.0018pp, p=0.0003). On the tape: a well-powered NULL across eight instruments on 65 release sessions since 2021 — SPY p=0.5820, QQQ p=0.8524, ITB p=0.2969, XHB p=0.2930, DHI p=0.5332, LEN p=0.8818, PHM p=0.8240, TOL p=0.2022, with the homebuilder ETFs actually NARROWER on release days. Census flags the headline m/m as not statistically significant in 37 of 40 measured editions; the median stated margin of error is +/-15.5% against a median |m/m| of 5.8%. Impact LOW, symbols empty: no house playbook is macro-keyed (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-06), and 2026-11-25 already carries four tracked events including two `high`-tier ones (gdp-q3-2026-second, pce).
